failedAssertions.reason: Persistence is correct (area_acme_main, duration 120 with a 120-minute occupancy, dietary tag, internal notes) and GET by id returns diningAreaId/durationMin/dietaryNotes/internalNotes, but the detail sheet renders neither the occasion nor the dining-area name (only the assigned table), the API returns the occasion as the resolved tag id `tag_acme_anniversary` instead of the chosen value `anniversary`, and the booking sheet has no free-text dietary-notes input so dietary text can only be written from tag codes.

The service selector updates the URL and re-fetches the day feed with `serviceId`, but the list never narrows: the tenant-api `/book/day` handler ignores `serviceId` (dayQuerySchema accepts only locationId/date/businessDate) and the client-side filter applies only status and search, so all 4 rows render in every mode. The Book page also renders no party/cover header counters at all.

Search works in all four required modes (name, middle phone digits, confirmation code, table label) and combines with status filters, but the area filter does not narrow the list (selecting Main Dining Room left rows from other areas) and no source (phone vs walk_in) or guest/reservation tag filter exists on the page - only the search input and status buttons are present.

The sheet renders guest identity, confirmation code, status, date/time/duration, party size, assigned table, notes and the CRM visit summary, but it renders no source/channel, no occasion, and audit entries without timestamps; it never loads the change history from `GET /operator/reservations/book/reservations/:id/events` (network capture shows only GET /reservations/:id and GET /book/day). The `/events` endpoint itself returns 200 with type/actorKind/at when called directly.

RTL and Arabic rendering are correct (dir=rtl, lang=ar, Arabic tabs/filters/quick actions, no raw message ids, LTR-correct confirmation codes/times/phones, no console errors), but status badges still render the raw English enums `booked`, `confirmed`, `arrived`, `seated`, `finished`, `no_show`, `cancelled` in the Arabic UI (apps/app/app/routes/_app+/$orgSlug_+/reservations+/today.tsx:376,507,590, book.tsx:449,453, detail-sheet.tsx:403).

(a) The block cannot be created through the UI (HTTP 500, see VAL-SETUP-023), so the blocks had to be created by API; (b) the soft booking was auto-reassigned to G4-1 with an `auto_reassigned` event carrying from/to table ids, but no move notice reaches hosts - the day feed has no `moveNotices` key and the timeline shows 'Automatic Reflow Notices 0'; (c) the locked booking on the blocked table was not moved but is not surfaced as unassigned/conflict anywhere in the timeline (badge 0), only in the settings conflicts endpoint as `blocked_table`; (d) the guest-side clause is not exercisable - tenant-api `/reservations/manage` and Sites `/reserve/manage` both 404 (belongs to milestone `guest-channels-and-crm`).

Engine I4 is not enforced for holds supplied through `existingHolds`: `searchAvailability` (packages/reservations/src/availability.ts:395-435) folds them into occupancies without filtering `expiresAt`, and the `kind === 'hold'` branch of the assignment path (packages/reservations/src/assign.ts:370-420) lacks the expiry filter that the separate `input.holds` loop applies at :414, so an expired hold keeps consuming capacity. The six gaps the previous round named are closed (24 engine tests, 71 package tests pass).

The sequence property suite verifies I1-I8 after every step and the day-scenario suite compares against the brute-force oracle, but the oracle runs once per day scenario, not after every step of `executeOperationSequence` (apps/tenant-api/src/services/engine.property.test.ts:45), while the assertion asks for zero soundness failures against the oracle after every step. Substance is verified (300 day scenarios, 100 operation sequences, per-step I1-I8, 200/2000/5000 caps, the four previously missing semantics); only the per-step oracle comparison for the sequence suite is missing. Test-side gap, not a product defect.

The booked path assigns correctly (drag onto M1 -> POST /assign 200, occupancy row for tbl_acme_m1, banner and canvas updated), but the arrived path does not: dropping an arrived, unassigned party on M2 (and `POST /status {status:'seated', tableIds:[tbl_acme_p3]}`) returns 200 and sets `seatedAt` yet creates no occupancy row, leaves the day feed at `tableIds: []` and keeps the table Available - the UI claims an assignment that was never persisted. `transitionReservationStatus` in apps/tenant-api/src/services/rsv-booking-service.ts ignores the `tableIds` the App sends.

Pacing-rule Delete from the UI returns 404: the client builds a location-scoped path `/locations/:id/pacing/:ruleId` (apps/app/app/utils/reservations/setup-api.ts:1958-1966) while tenant-api registers DELETE only at `/pacing/:id` (apps/tenant-api/src/routes/operator-reservations-setup.ts:1482-1507). Create via the UI, update/delete via API, and cap enforcement (409 pacing_exceeded) all pass.

Service-availability Delete from the UI returns 404 (same path-shape mismatch: setup-api.ts:2045-2053 vs operator-reservations-setup.ts:1644-1649). All four modes persist, XOR target validation returns 400 for zero or two targets, and PUT/DELETE via API return 200.

Creating a block from the UI always fails with HTTP 500: the form posts `startMin`/`endMin` and `createBlockForLocation` assigns a `localToInstant()` resolution object into the numeric `start_at`/`end_at` columns (apps/tenant-api/src/services/rsv-setup-crud.ts:3049-3056). API create with epoch `startAt`/`endAt`, area expansion, reflow and delete all pass; Vitest reservations-setup.test.ts 8/8 passes.

The endpoint half passes (401 without a token, 200 with items enriched with `details.businessDate`, Vitest 8/8), but the conflicts panel on /acme/reservations/settings fails: with 5 real conflicts it rendered every row as '· (p)' - no confirmation code, no date, no party size and an empty reason badge. The panel reads `confirmationCode/businessDate/partySize/reason` (apps/app/app/utils/reservations/setup-api.ts:124-141, apps/app/app/routes/_app+/$orgSlug_+/reservations+/settings._index.tsx:855-876) while the API returns `kind/bookingId/tableId|serviceId/details.businessDate`, and `fetchSetupConflicts` raw-casts the response with no mapping.

appliedUpdates.description: Added the round foh-core block: verified environment state, the operator-token minting helper (/tmp/menuza-user-testing/mint-token.mjs, secret from apps/app/.dev.vars, issuer 'menuza'), the per-group data-isolation registry, setup-mutation isolation rules, Flow Validator Guidance sections for terminal/curl/agent-browser/restricted accounts, and the batch A-E concurrency plan.

Appended round results and runtime findings: the local-D1 system-level reservations.enabled=true row (deleting org rows does not hide the module; ~40 s watchdog restores rows), the invite/signup recipe corrections (Verification has no code column, compute the TOTP locally; Create Link always mints the built-in Member role), the curated settings form (18 PUT-only fields), agent-browser drag/fill quirks, the fact that public availability and guest-manage routes are not implemented in foh-core, a defect table with root cause file:line for all 13 failing assertions, and the contract-vs-implementation terminology deviations.

No corrections needed: every start/stop/healthcheck/seed command in services.yaml worked as written this round (App 3001 via VITE_DIRECT_DEV=1, Sites 3008 via PUBLIC_APP_URL, tenant-api US 3007 / KSA 3009, seed:reservations + seed:guests for acme and riyadh-grill).

flagStateAfterRun.note: No validator changed a flag permanently. acme and riyadh-grill org rows are all true after the round; g17 induced the module-off state for ~42 s with the org-level row (the local D1 system row is true, so deleting rows would not have hidden the module) and restored it.
flagStateAfterRun.system_level_row_note: packages/database/db/data.db has reservations.enabled=false for the system row; apps/app/.wrangler/state (local D1) has true. The contract's flag-off precondition therefore does not hold locally until that row is written to false.

servicesAfterRun: App dev (3001) and Sites (3008) were started by this validator and are stopped during teardown. tenant-api US (3007) and KSA (3009) were already running before this session (started by an earlier session) and were left untouched. Admin (3005) was not needed and stayed stopped.
knownDeferredItemsConfirmed: The guest-facing clause of VAL-CROSS-006 (guest manage view must not show table reassignments) is not exercisable: tenant-api /reservations/manage and Sites /reserve/manage both 404 in this milestone; the public availability/manage routes belong to guest-channels-and-crm. Reported as blocked evidence inside the failed assertion, not as a product defect.
VAL-FND-009's per-step oracle comparison is a test-side gap, not user-visible behavior; the assertion's substantive semantics were re-verified as non-vacuous this round.

Contract-vs-implementation naming deviations recorded (not failures): rsv_reservation_tables -> rsv_table_occupancies; locked_assignment -> rsv_reservations.assignment; event names table_assigned -> table_changed/locked/unlocked, undone -> status_undo; idempotency scopes are route paths; replay answers 201; full-slot code tables_occupied; course event type course.

Observed but not adjudicated as a failure of an assignment: the sidebar renders Waitlist for the Host-preset role (contract text for VAL-CROSS-002 says 'only Today and Book', but the waitlist link shares read:reservation:any and none of the forbidden surfaces appear); Settings > Services renders only a curated subset of the settings fields, so UI assertions about the other 18 fields are unsatisfiable by construction; deleting a location leaves its regional tenant rows behind (deleteScopeData only clears phone-agent data).
overrideJustification: No user-authorized deferrals were applied this round. Two adjudications by the synthesizer, both documented in validation-state.json issues: (1) VAL-SETUP-025 was reported 'pass' by its flow group for the endpoint half, but the same report and a second independent group both show the conflicts panel rendering rows as '· (p)' from an unmapped payload, so the assertion's UI clause ('lists each conflict with its date and reason code') is marked failed; (2) VAL-FND-006 and VAL-FND-009 stay failed as reported, with VAL-FND-009's reason narrowed to the missing per-step oracle comparison so the orchestrator can choose between fixing the test and amending the assertion.
